references.summary: Web Security Testing Guide methodology and test case structure.

references.name: OWASP ASVS
references.summary: Application Security Verification Standard requirements for web apps and APIs.

references.name: OWASP Top 10 2025
references.summary: Current released OWASP Top 10 web application risk categories.

phases.title: Scope and Rules
phases.objective: Confirm written authorization, target boundaries, test windows, accounts, rate limits, and emergency contacts before any active testing.
tasks: Save authorization, scope, exclusions, and testing window.
List allowed domains, IP ranges, API base URLs, mobile apps, and third-party services.
Confirm whether authenticated testing, social engineering, denial-of-service testing, and destructive checks are excluded.
Create an evidence folder with timestamps, screenshots, request IDs, and command output.

phases.title: Map the Application
phases.objective: Build a clean inventory of routes, technologies, roles, authentication flows, input points, files, and APIs.
tasks: Browse the application manually as each approved role and record major workflows.
Capture sitemap data with a proxy such as ZAP or Burp on an authorized test account.
Fingerprint server, framework, headers, cookies, TLS posture, and exposed metadata.
Separate public, authenticated, administrative, and API attack surfaces.

phases.title: Auth and Session
phases.objective: Check identity, password reset, MFA, session lifetime, cookie flags, logout behavior, and account recovery controls.
tasks: Verify login, logout, password reset, account recovery, and MFA flows for approved accounts.
Check cookie flags, session rotation after login, and invalidation after logout or password change.
Confirm lockout, throttling, and user enumeration behavior without brute force.
Record all account and role combinations used during testing.

phases.title: Access Control
phases.objective: Verify that users cannot access another role's data, actions, direct object references, or administrative paths.
tasks: Create a role matrix for every approved test account.
Replay authorized requests across lower-privilege roles and confirm server-side denial.
Check object IDs, account IDs, organization IDs, and tenant IDs for missing authorization checks.
Capture both the allowed request and the denied request as evidence.

phases.title: Input and Injection
phases.objective: Review input handling for injection, validation gaps, reflected output, file parsing, command execution, and unsafe deserialization.
tasks: Map every parameter, header, file upload field, JSON field, and GraphQL variable.
Use non-destructive scanner checks first and confirm findings with minimal safe proof.
Look for stack traces, database errors, template errors, unexpected redirects, and reflected output.
Document validation rules and remediation without publishing dangerous payloads.

phases.title: API and Data Flow
phases.objective: Assess API authentication, authorization, schemas, rate limits, errors, CORS, sensitive data exposure, and mass assignment risk.
tasks: Collect OpenAPI, GraphQL schema, Postman collections, and mobile/API endpoints if authorized.
Check each method for authentication, authorization, input validation, and clear error behavior.
Compare server responses against expected schemas and data minimization rules.
Verify CORS only allows approved origins and sensitive methods are protected.

phases.title: Configuration and Supply Chain
phases.objective: Review security headers, TLS, dependency risk, exposed files, CI/CD secrets, container posture, and logging coverage.
tasks: Check security headers and cookie attributes from public and authenticated areas.
Run dependency, secret, container, and repository scans against approved code or build artifacts.
Review exposed files such as backups, debug endpoints, source maps, and environment leaks.
Confirm logs capture security-relevant events without storing secrets.

phases.title: Validate and Report
phases.objective: Turn verified findings into clear risk statements, proof, impact, remediation, and retest steps.
tasks: Deduplicate scanner results and remove unverified noise.
Assign severity from impact and likelihood, not tool labels alone.
Write every finding with affected asset, steps to reproduce, evidence, impact, remediation, and retest guidance.
Include positive controls and items that were out of scope.

matrix.name: Broken Access Control
checks: Role matrix covers every protected workflow.
Direct object references are denied across accounts and tenants.
Admin-only endpoints reject low-privilege users on the server.
matrix.report: Show the allowed request, the unauthorized request, expected denial, and actual response.

matrix.name: Injection
checks: Inputs are mapped across query strings, JSON, forms, headers, and uploads.
Unexpected errors, reflected output, and unsafe interpreter behavior are investigated safely.
Scanner findings are manually verified without destructive commands.
matrix.report: Include affected parameter, request, response behavior, impact, and safe remediation.

matrix.name: Security Misconfiguration
checks: Debug pages, default credentials, directory listing, backups, and verbose errors are absent.
Security headers and cookie flags meet the app's risk profile.
Cloud storage, API gateways, and reverse proxies enforce intended access.
matrix.report: List exposed setting, affected URL, evidence, and exact configuration fix.

matrix.name: Vulnerable Components
checks: Lockfiles, containers, and source repositories are scanned.
Findings are matched to reachable code paths and deployed versions.
Upgrade, patch, or compensating control is documented.
matrix.report: Tie CVE, package, installed version, fixed version, reachability, and owner.

matrix.name: Identification and Authentication Failures
checks: MFA, recovery, password change, and logout flows are verified.
Session tokens rotate after login and are invalidated after logout.
Lockout and throttling work without allowing user enumeration.
matrix.report: Include user journey, headers, token behavior, and affected account conditions.

matrix.name: Sensitive Data Exposure
checks: Responses do not leak tokens, secrets, PII, internal IDs, or stack traces.
TLS and HSTS are configured for production surfaces.
Logs and analytics avoid storing credentials or session material.
matrix.report: Redact sensitive values while proving data type, location, and access path.

matrix.name: File Upload Risk
checks: Uploads enforce allowed file types, size limits, malware scanning, and storage isolation.
Uploaded content is served with safe content type and no execution.
Metadata and image processing errors do not leak internals.
matrix.report: Show upload policy gap, server behavior, storage path exposure, and fix.

matrix.name: Logging and Monitoring Gaps
checks: Authentication, access control denials, admin actions, and suspicious validation failures are logged.
Alerts exist for high-risk events and unusual volume.
Logs are protected from tampering and sensitive data leakage.
matrix.report: Show missing event, expected detection, business risk, and logging requirement.
